paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: Comparison of the Improvement for 5-digit and 6-digit multiplication with as feedback model
model_annotation: The line plot titled “Accuracy Improvement Over Iterations” illustrates the progression of accuracy (%) for two tasks—5-digit and 6-digit multiplication—across nine iterations, presumably as a feedback model is applied. The x-axis, labeled “Iteration,” spans from 0 to 9 with integer tick marks at each unit, indicating discrete steps in the feedback process. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, ranges from 0 to 100 with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 20 (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). Two lines are plotted: the blue line with circular markers represents the 6-digit task, starting at approximately 3% accuracy at iteration 0, rising sharply to 37% at iteration 1, then increasing more gradually to 90% by iteration 9. The orange line with square markers represents the 5-digit task, beginning at about 2% at iteration 0, jumping to 68% at iteration 1, and then rising steadily to 90% by iteration 9. Both lines converge near 90% accuracy by the final iteration, with the 5-digit task showing a steeper initial gain but slightly slower growth thereafter compared to the 6-digit task after iteration 2.
